published.name: mcp_guide
published.title: Tool guide
published.description: Describes the tools this user can call. Without arguments it lists every module available and the tools of each one; with module it details every tool of that module; with tool it details a single tool. Use it before acting with a tool you do not already know. Reads only: it changes nothing.

module.description: Module to detail. Call the guide without arguments to see the modules available to this user.

tool.description: Single tool to detail, by its technical name (for example files_edit). Takes precedence over module.

published.name: files_list
published.title: List files
published.description: List files and folders from a user Nextcloud directory.

path.description: Path of the file or folder, e.g. /Documents/report.pdf

published.name: files_search
published.title: Search files
published.description: Search files by name or indexed content in the user folder on Nextcloud; when permitted, stored file descriptions are searched too.

query.description: Search term to find in file names or indexed content, and in stored file descriptions when permitted.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100, default 25).

mode.description: Search mode: "auto" uses full-text content search when available, falls back to name search, and includes matching stored descriptions when permitted. Results report content_and_description or name_and_description when descriptions are searched; "name" searches only file names.

published.name: files_tree
published.title: View folder tree
published.description: List the file tree of a folder, with the owner of each item and capacity limits. Use to plan a reorganization without one call per folder. Enforces depth and entry limits, and warns when truncated.

path.description: Path of the file or folder, e.g. /Documents/report.pdf

published.name: files_read
published.title: Read file
published.description: Read the text of a file from Nextcloud (plain text/markdown directly; PDF/DOCX/ODT via text extraction).

path.description: Path of the file or folder, e.g. /Documents/report.pdf

published.name: files_versions_list
published.title: List file versions
published.description: List versions of a file from the Versions app, from newest to oldest.

path.description: Path of the file or folder, e.g. /Documents/report.pdf

published.name: files_version_read
published.title: Read file version
published.description: Read the text of a previous file version, with the same limit and text extraction as files_read.

path.description: Path of the file or folder, e.g. /Documents/report.pdf

version.description: Version identifier, as returned by files_versions_list

published.name: files_image_view
published.title: View image
published.description: Fetch a reduced preview of an image file as inline image bytes, so the model can actually see it. Reads only; honors the user folder and permissions. Supports JPG, PNG, HEIC, WebP, GIF, TIFF and the first page of a PDF when the Nextcloud server has a preview provider for the format. The returned image is JPEG/PNG/WebP under a server-wide byte limit: if the preview is still too big the max dimension is reduced until it fits.

path.description: Path of the file or folder, e.g. /Documents/report.pdf

max_size.description: Maximum width or height of the returned preview, in pixels (256-2048, default 1568)

published.name: files_images_view
published.title: View several images
published.description: Fetch several image previews in a single call. Pass either paths (up to 6 items) or folder (plus an optional limit) to pick the most recently modified images under that folder. The total image bytes stay under a server-wide budget; images that do not fit are reported as skipped with the reason, so the agent knows what was left out.

folder.description: Folder to look in, e.g. /Photos; omit to search the whole user folder

max_size.description: Maximum width or height of the returned preview, in pixels (256-2048, default 1568)

published.name: files_image_search
published.title: Search images
published.description: Search image files in the user folder, optionally filtered by name query, folder, modification date range or system tag name (the tag names created by the Recognize app count too). Results are listed newest first and only contain the file metadata; use files_image_view to fetch bytes.

query.description: Optional name substring, e.g. "beach"

folder.description: Folder to look in, e.g. /Photos; omit to search the whole user folder

modified_after.description: ISO 8601 date or datetime, only images modified at or after this moment are returned

modified_before.description: ISO 8601 date or datetime, only images modified at or before this moment are returned

tag.description: System tag name (case-sensitive), including automatic tags created by the Recognize app

published.name: files_list_shares
published.title: List shares
published.description: List the shares you created: with a path, your shares on that file or folder, including your public links on items you can re-share; without one, every share you created, 50 per page with offset. Each item has shareId, type (user, group, link or room), with (id and display name), permission (view, edit or custom), reshare, expires, hasPassword, url (links only; null for a folder link while files are excluded from MCP access), removable and path. Passwords are never returned. A room share is a Talk attachment: it is listed with removable: false and is removed in Talk.

path.description: File or folder whose shares to list, e.g. /Documents/report.pdf. Omit to list every share you created.

offset.description: Shares to skip when listing without path; use the nextOffset of the previous page.

published.name: notes_list
published.title: List notes
published.description: Lists the notes (Notes app) of the user.

published.name: notes_search
published.title: Search notes
published.description: Searches notes by title and content (Markdown).

query.description: Search term to find in note title or content.

limit.description: Maximum number of notes to return (1-100, default 20).

category.description: Optional category (subfolder) to limit search to; empty for all notes.

published.name: notes_read
published.title: Read note
published.description: Reads the content of a note by id.

published.name: calendar_list_calendars
published.title: List calendars
published.description: Lists calendars visible to the user.

published.name: calendar_list_events
published.title: List events
published.description: Lists events in a time range (default: next 7 days).

calendar.description: calendar path (optional)

from.description: start ISO date

published.name: contacts_list_addressbooks
published.title: List address books
published.description: List your own and shared address books plus, when the admin exposes it, the read-only accounts catalog of the instance.

published.name: contacts_search_contacts
published.title: Search contacts
published.description: Search contacts by name, email, phone or organization in one address book or, when "addressbook" is omitted, in all of them including the read-only accounts of the instance (colleagues). Account results carry accountId, the user ID to use for invitations, attendees, Deck and Talk. An empty query lists personal contacts only; accounts need a search term of at least 2 characters.

addressbook.description: Address book path returned by List address books. Omit to search all of them.

query.description: Case-insensitive search text.

limit.description: Maximum results (1-200).

offset.description: Offset among matching results; use nextOffset to continue.

published.name: contacts_read_contact
published.title: Read contact
published.description: Read a contact including all vCard properties and its ETag. A contact of the accounts catalog returns only its public fields and accountId, without vCard or ETag.

addressbook.description: Address book path returned by List address books.

uri.description: Contact object URI returned by Search contacts.

published.name: tasks_list_calendars
published.title: List task calendars
published.description: List your own and shared calendars supporting tasks (VTODO).

published.name: tasks_list_tasks
published.title: List tasks
published.description: List tasks, including undated tasks, in one visible task calendar, optionally only those with a category or only the subtasks of one task.

calendar.description: VTODO calendar path from List task calendars.

category.description: Literal category label to match exactly, ignoring case. Omit this field to list tasks without a category filter.

parent.description: Only list the direct subtasks of the task with this UID. Omit the field to list every task.

limit.description: Maximum results (1-200).

offset.description: Offset among matching results; use nextOffset to continue.

published.name: tasks_read_task
published.title: Read task
published.description: Read a task by its UID in a visible task calendar.

calendar.description: VTODO calendar path from List task calendars.

published.name: deck_list_boards
published.title: List Deck boards
published.description: Lists the Deck boards shared with you, excluding archived ones.

published.name: deck_list_stacks
published.title: List Deck lists
published.description: Lists the lists (stacks) of a Deck board, with the number of cards in each.

published.name: deck_list_cards
published.title: List Deck cards
published.description: Lists the active cards of a Deck list (stack), paginated.

limit.description: Maximum number of cards to return.

offset.description: Number of cards to skip, for pagination.

published.name: deck_read_card
published.title: Read Deck card
published.description: Reads a Deck card with its description, dates and counters.

published.name: deck_followup_cards
published.title: Follow up on Deck tasks
published.description: Lists the cards of the boards you can manage (owner or manage permission), grouped by assignee, with a direct link to each card. By default it returns only overdue cards; the scan covers at most 100 visible boards.

status.description: Status filter: overdue (due before today), open, done or all. Default: overdue.

assignee.description: UID of the assignee (if you are not sure of someone's ID, call users_search first); returns only the cards assigned to that person.

dueBefore.description: Returns only cards due on or before this date, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

limit.description: Maximum number of cards to return.

published.name: deck_list_labels
published.title: List Deck labels
published.description: Lists the labels available on a readable Deck board, with their IDs, titles and colours. Available on Nextcloud 32 through 35 when Deck is enabled.

limit.description: Page size.

offset.description: Offset.

published.name: deck_list_card_files
published.title: List Deck card files
published.description: Lists only visible existing native file associations of a readable Deck card. Requires deck.read and files.read, Files resource scope, exclusion tags and native node READ. No legacy deck_file or folders, no upload, no hidden count/handle; IDs are association/share IDs distinct from fileId. All visible items ordered by attachmentId; native Card attachmentCount stays omitted. Available on Nextcloud 32 through 35. An association you cannot see is omitted and answered like a missing one. Open the card in Deck without treating that answer as proof that a hidden association exists.

published.name: talk_list_conversations
published.title: List Talk conversations
published.description: Lists the Talk conversations the authenticated user takes part in, with the number of unread messages. It changes no state: it does not mark anything as read, does not touch notifications and does not touch activity.

published.name: talk_read_messages
published.title: Read Talk messages
published.description: Reads conversation messages without changing read or notification state or recording activity. Each page is ordered oldest-to-newest and includes messages plus next_before_message_id. Start without before_message_id; use the returned next_before_message_id as the exclusive before_message_id for older history. The cursor is null when no older page remains. Use a message id in reply_to to answer, and attachmentId to cite an attachment.

before_message_id.description: Return messages older than this ID, exclusive; use next_before_message_id from the previous page.

published.name: users_search
published.title: Search people
published.description: Searches the accounts of this Nextcloud by name, account ID or e-mail and returns their account IDs (uid), display names and, when available, e-mail; every row carries a type, "user" for an account. Use it whenever you are not sure of someone's account ID. Groups are not searched by default: to also match groups, pass include_groups: true, and the group rows come back with the type "group" and the group ID, which is what a share takes as group:<id>.

query.description: Name, account ID or e-mail to look for (2 to 100 characters).

limit.description: Maximum number of accounts returned (default 10, at most 25).

include_groups.description: Also match groups, for sharing with a group: they come back with the type "group" and the group ID (default false).

content.text:
This guide is in English: relay it to the user in their own language.

Write confirmation plans arrive as readable text in the user’s language, with the complete plan in structuredContent. Show that text to the user exactly as received.

# Tool guide

Grants and disabled apps are already applied: what is missing from this list you cannot call. The modules available to you are files, notes, calendar, contacts, tasks, deck, talk, people.

- **Files** (`files`): 10 tools — List files, Search files, View folder tree, Read file, List file versions, Read file version, View image, View several images, Search images, List shares.
- **Notes** (`notes`): 3 tools — List notes, Search notes, Read note.
- **Calendar** (`calendar`): 2 tools — List calendars, List events.
- **Contacts** (`contacts`): 3 tools — List address books, Search contacts, Read contact.
- **Tasks** (`tasks`): 3 tools — List task calendars, List tasks, Read task.
- **Deck** (`deck`): 7 tools — List Deck boards, List Deck lists, List Deck cards, Read Deck card, Follow up on Deck tasks, List Deck labels, List Deck card files.
- **Talk** (`talk`): 2 tools — List Talk conversations, Read Talk messages.
- **People** (`people`): 1 tools — Search people.

Call this tool again with `module` set to one of those names to get every parameter and every behaviour note of that module, or with `tool` to detail a single tool.

structuredContent.language_note: This guide is in English: relay it to the user in their own language.

modules.title: Files
notes: Paths are absolute inside the folder of the user calling and start at "/"; they are never relative and never leave the storage Nextcloud already lets that user reach.

To find something, use files_search for full-text content search when available (or by file name), files_tree for the shape of a folder (depth 5, 2000 entries) and files_list for a single folder. The `access` field of every entry says who owns it and what it allows.
Reorganization is the only way files change places: a copy is capped at 2000 items and 1 GiB, a batch takes at most 200 moves, and nothing overwrites the destination.
Pass `etag` when changing what was just read: a different etag aborts the write instead of dropping the change someone else made in the meantime.

Anything outside the personal folder is refused on a write until the user has been asked and the call repeats with confirm_shared: true. A calendar, a share or a file owned by somebody else is that case.

files_edit, files_replace and files_checkout need versioning on (files_versions). MCP pre-write copies default on in the configured backup folder; administrators may suspend them while Versions is enabled for the actor. Native versioning follows its own policy and does not guarantee recovery. files_checkout hands out short-lived links for local tools instead of passing the content through the model.

files_edit and files_replace change text files only. Use files_checkout for any file type up to the upload limit (docx, xlsx, pdf, images): download, edit locally, upload the whole file back. A scanned PDF is regenerated by the client from what it read, never edited byte by byte.

To create a NEW file generated locally (docx, xlsx, pdf, image, any type), use files_upload: confirm it, then send the bytes with curl -sS -T /tmp/file -X PUT -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" "$UPLOAD_URL" to the single-use uploadUrl it returns (15 minutes, the same limit as files_checkout). For a small text file (.md, .txt, .csv, .json, .html, .xml, .yaml) use files_create with the content inline, up to 1 MB. Neither ever overwrites a file with content: to replace an existing file use files_checkout. The folder must already exist (files_mkdir).

files_read and files_version_read of a PDF or image with no text return text_layer: false and a notice instead of an error: the file is a scan. If the Workflow OCR app is active it recognises the text in the background (by the administrator's rule) and writes it into the PDF as a new version, so read again later; otherwise view the page as an image with the image tools.

There is no delete: files_undo_batch is the way back from files_move_batch, and files_version_restore writes the content of a stored version back over the file, applying the administrator backup setting.

files_share shares a file or folder of yours with a person (with: user:<uid>) or a group (group:<gid>); find the id with users_search (include_groups: true for groups) and never guess it. Sharing again with the same recipient changes that share; the plan shows before → after, including a re-share right a web-made share loses. Nextcloud notifies the recipient. with: "link" is the public link of the file (needs the "link" permission). For a read or upload link, use custom_password only for a value supplied by the user. A generated password is shown once in the confirmed result. Confirm with the plan_state of the plan: when the share changed in the meantime, nothing is written and the answer is the new plan to show again.

files_list_shares shows only shares you created. On items shared with you, you can manage your own public links when Nextcloud permits re-sharing and downloads. A password is never shown, only hasPassword. A room share is a Talk attachment and is removed in Talk. Sharing with people or groups needs the "share" permission and public links the separate "link" permission, both granted by the administrator.

files_unshare removes one share you created (by the shareId of files_list_shares, or by path plus with); the plan says who loses access, and the file itself is never touched. It cannot remove what somebody else shared or an internal share on a received item. Remove Talk attachments in Talk. Confirm with the plan_state of the plan, as for files_share.

tools.title: View folder tree
tools.description: List the file tree of a folder, with the owner of each item and capacity limits. Use to plan a reorganization without one call per folder. Enforces depth and entry limits, and warns when truncated.

tools.name: files_read
tools.title: Read file
tools.description: Read the text of a file from Nextcloud (plain text/markdown directly; PDF/DOCX/ODT via text extraction).

tools.name: files_versions_list
tools.title: List file versions
tools.description: List versions of a file from the Versions app, from newest to oldest.

tools.name: files_version_read
tools.title: Read file version
tools.description: Read the text of a previous file version, with the same limit and text extraction as files_read.

tools.name: files_image_view
tools.title: View image
tools.description: Fetch a reduced preview of an image file as inline image bytes, so the model can actually see it. Reads only; honors the user folder and permissions. Supports JPG, PNG, HEIC, WebP, GIF, TIFF and the first page of a PDF when the Nextcloud server has a preview provider for the format. The returned image is JPEG/PNG/WebP under a server-wide byte limit: if the preview is still too big the max dimension is reduced until it fits.

tools.name: files_images_view
tools.title: View several images
tools.description: Fetch several image previews in a single call. Pass either paths (up to 6 items) or folder (plus an optional limit) to pick the most recently modified images under that folder. The total image bytes stay under a server-wide budget; images that do not fit are reported as skipped with the reason, so the agent knows what was left out.

tools.name: files_image_search
tools.title: Search images
tools.description: Search image files in the user folder, optionally filtered by name query, folder, modification date range or system tag name (the tag names created by the Recognize app count too). Results are listed newest first and only contain the file metadata; use files_image_view to fetch bytes.

tools.name: files_list_shares
tools.title: List shares
tools.description: List the shares you created: with a path, your shares on that file or folder, including your public links on items you can re-share; without one, every share you created, 50 per page with offset. Each item has shareId, type (user, group, link or room), with (id and display name), permission (view, edit or custom), reshare, expires, hasPassword, url (links only; null for a folder link while files are excluded from MCP access), removable and path. Passwords are never returned. A room share is a Talk attachment: it is listed with removable: false and is removed in Talk.

modules.title: Notes
notes: A note is addressed by the `id` notes_list or notes_search returns, not by its title; the title is the file name and the category is the subfolder it sits in.
Use notes_search to find notes by keyword in title or Markdown content.
notes_create never overwrites: when the title is taken in that category it picks a free name, and the response says which name it used.
notes_delete only deletes where the Nextcloud trash bin takes the note back; anywhere else it refuses instead of removing it for good.
Notes are capped at 1048576 bytes read or written, and a title at 200 characters.
notes_edit accepts only one of content, append or old/new; append adds a line and old/new replaces one unique passage. Partial edits need the etag and plan_state from a fresh plan when confirmed.
Pass `etag` to make a change fail instead of overwriting somebody else's version of the same note.
Some notes or categories may be hidden by administrator policy and will appear as if they do not exist.

tools.name: notes_list
tools.title: List notes
tools.description: Lists the notes (Notes app) of the user.

tools.name: notes_search
tools.title: Search notes
tools.description: Searches notes by title and content (Markdown).

tools.name: notes_read
tools.title: Read note
tools.description: Reads the content of a note by id.

modules.title: Calendar
notes: Calendars are addressed by path: calendar_list_calendars gives the paths of this user. Events are addressed by uid, and calendar_list_events gives the uids of a period.

calendar_check_availability reads busy intervals and free ranges in an explicit UTC window of at most 31 days. It checks at most 20 visible calendars and returns no event titles. Private or unreadable event data, a scan limit, or any incomplete scan makes the whole answer unavailable rather than claiming a time is free.

Every write answers with a plan first: what it would change, the etag of the object as it is now, and which invitations would go out. Nothing is written until the very same call is repeated with confirm: true, so show the plan to the user and wait for an explicit yes.

The plan of a create, update (when the time or the guests change), move or transfer can carry warnings: a collision with another event of the target calendar, a participant who is busy or whose agenda could not be checked, and a calendar that is not shared with the participants. Each warning has a type (collision, busy, unverifiable, calendarNotShared) and a message to read to the user. They never block: tell the user and repeat the call with confirm: true only if the answer is still yes. When sharedCalendars lists calendars the participants already see and suggestedCalendar is set, offer it; when there are several, ask the user which one to use and repeat the call with that calendar. Other people's appointments are only ever reported as busy, never with their content. When an update moves an event, the event's own slot is left out of the availability check of the guests it already has (their copy of the invitation would otherwise make them busy); the collision check always leaves the event itself out. An appointment of a guest sitting entirely inside the old slot is not reported.
Dates and times arrive as they will be stored, and are read back in the timezone of the account; a recurring event is expanded into its occurrences before it reaches the user.

send_invitations hands the invitation to the CalDAV scheduling of the server. The plan and the result say whether the server has e-mail invitations switched on (imipEnabled); when it is off, say so to the user instead of claiming an e-mail was sent.
A calendar owned by somebody else (a share) needs confirm_shared after asking the user, and a transfer moves the event there and removes it from here.
A deleted event goes to the Nextcloud trash bin of the calendar; with retention at 0 the deletion is refused rather than permanent.
The writing tools appear only when the administrator granted them to this user; a module showing reads only means the writing grants are off.

tools.name: calendar_list_calendars
tools.title: List calendars
tools.description: Lists calendars visible to the user.

tools.name: calendar_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: Lists events in a time range (default: next 7 days).

modules.title: Contacts
notes: List address books first; your own and shared address books are exposed, plus the read-only accounts catalog when the admin allows it. Searching without an address book also covers the accounts of the instance (colleagues, with a term of at least 2 characters, following the admin user-enumeration settings); each account result has accountId, the ID to use for invitations. Use users_search to look for accounts only. Account contacts can never be created, edited or deleted.
Search an address book to obtain contact object URIs, then read a contact before editing it. Unknown vCard properties are preserved; the preview includes every property before and after.

Writes first show a plan without changing anything. Wait for an explicit yes, repeat with confirm=true, and acknowledge another owner with confirm_shared=true. The optional etag prevents overwriting a newer edit.

Contact deletion is PERMANENT in Nextcloud: there is no contact trash. After confirmation, a verified full .vcf copy is saved under Contacts in the configured backup folder before native CardDAV DELETE. Backup failure prevents deletion; the result gives the backup path. Import the .vcf through Contacts to recover it.
These tools are hidden when the Contacts app is disabled. Writing grants start disabled.

tools.name: contacts_list_addressbooks
tools.title: List address books
tools.description: List your own and shared address books plus, when the admin exposes it, the read-only accounts catalog of the instance.

tools.name: contacts_search_contacts
tools.title: Search contacts
tools.description: Search contacts by name, email, phone or organization in one address book or, when "addressbook" is omitted, in all of them including the read-only accounts of the instance (colleagues). Account results carry accountId, the user ID to use for invitations, attendees, Deck and Talk. An empty query lists personal contacts only; accounts need a search term of at least 2 characters.

tools.name: contacts_read_contact
tools.title: Read contact
tools.description: Read a contact including all vCard properties and its ETag. A contact of the accounts catalog returns only its public fields and accountId, without vCard or ETag.

modules.title: Tasks
notes: Task calendars support VTODO. These tools require the Tasks app and core CalDAV. List task calendars before addressing a task by UID.

Undated tasks are included. Completed tasks are hidden by default in listings. Recurring tasks can be read; changing recurring tasks or tasks with participants is refused to protect their series and scheduling.

Task categories are free text, as in the Tasks app. On create and edit, a categories list replaces all existing categories, [] clears them and omitting the field preserves them. tasks_list_tasks can filter by one category, ignoring case.

Subtasks link to their parent by UID (RELATED-TO), as in the Tasks app, and every task returns its parent UID or null. On create and edit, parent sets it, null makes the task top-level and omitting it preserves it; the parent must be a visible task of the same calendar and cannot be the task or one of its subtasks, and no task may end up deeper than 64 levels, the moved subtasks included. tasks_list_tasks with parent lists the direct subtasks. Deleting or completing a parent does not change its subtasks. The hierarchy is checked on the state read when the plan is built and again at confirmation; confirmed MCP writes that set a parent in one calendar run one at a time (they are refused when the file locking of the server is disabled), but other clients can still change related tasks at the same moment, and an answer with a warning says that the parent chain then loops.
Private and confidential tasks in shared calendars are hidden. Writable shares require confirm_shared=true after showing the owner notice.
Every write starts with a before/after plan. Wait for explicit approval before confirm=true; the optional etag checks for concurrent edits. Writing grants start disabled.
Deletion uses the native calendar trash and is refused when calendar retention is zero. The result confirms recovery through the calendar trash.

tools.name: tasks_list_calendars
tools.title: List task calendars
tools.description: List your own and shared calendars supporting tasks (VTODO).

tools.name: tasks_list_tasks
tools.title: List tasks
tools.description: List tasks, including undated tasks, in one visible task calendar, optionally only those with a category or only the subtasks of one task.

tools.name: tasks_read_task
tools.title: Read task
tools.description: Read a task by its UID in a visible task calendar.

modules.title: Deck
notes: A card is addressed by three ids: deck_list_boards gives the board, deck_list_stacks the lists of a board, and deck_list_cards the cards of a list. Read them in that order before writing anything.
deck_read_card returns the card with its comments; deck_followup_cards lists the cards that are due or overdue, per board.

A board owned by somebody else is refused on a write until the user has been asked and the call repeats with confirm_shared: true. The refusal is a normal result that says what is missing, not an error.

The caller owns a created card. Explicit assignments are checked before creation and shown in the plan. Assignment changes during creation can produce a created card with warnings; read it before retrying in Deck. deck_edit_card changes assignees with assign and unassign (lists of account IDs, at most 100 each); an account cannot be in both, accounts are checked before anything is written, and a failure midway leaves the result listing assigned, unassigned and failed.

To set up a project from scratch use one deck_create_board call: it creates the board, its lists and their first cards after a single confirmation (at most 20 lists and 100 cards). The board is open only to its owner, so share it in Deck before assigning anybody else. deck_create_stack adds a list to an existing board. deck_delete_stack and deck_delete_board work only on something empty: they refuse, saying how many cards are left, while any card (active or archived) remains, and what they delete goes to the Deck trash. A card created by somebody else right after the second count they take before finishing may go to the trash with the list or board; it is recoverable there.

duedate accepts YYYY-MM-DD (local midnight), YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS] in the account timezone, or a timestamp with Z/±HH:MM. Nonexistent local times are refused; repeated local times use the first occurrence. Output duedate remains the local date and dueAt gives the instant with the account offset, without a timezone field. overdue is based on the local day, not the time; dueBefore accepts only YYYY-MM-DD.
Older affected deadlines must be corrected manually after checking the intended date in Deck; existing stored instants are never shifted automatically.
A card description is capped at 100000 characters and a title at 255.
deck_move_card can reorder a card within its current list or move it to another list, including one on another board. Set stackId to the destination list; without order, the card goes to the end.

deck_link_card_file requires deck.edit, files.read and files.share. Its approved plan grants native read-only file access to current and future board/group/team members. It refuses unsupported sharing policies or incomplete audiences; later membership/policy changes and the final native-write race are not continuously enforced or automatically revoked.

Use deck_list_labels before incremental add/remove label edits; repeat plan_state after approval. Unlinking a visible native file association can remove another editor’s association and the access/mount it provides, including your last mount. The file itself remains; recovery may require the native Deck UI.

tools.name: deck_list_boards
tools.title: List Deck boards
tools.description: Lists the Deck boards shared with you, excluding archived ones.

tools.name: deck_list_stacks
tools.title: List Deck lists
tools.description: Lists the lists (stacks) of a Deck board, with the number of cards in each.

tools.name: deck_list_cards
tools.title: List Deck cards
tools.description: Lists the active cards of a Deck list (stack), paginated.

tools.name: deck_read_card
tools.title: Read Deck card
tools.description: Reads a Deck card with its description, dates and counters.

tools.name: deck_followup_cards
tools.title: Follow up on Deck tasks
tools.description: Lists the cards of the boards you can manage (owner or manage permission), grouped by assignee, with a direct link to each card. By default it returns only overdue cards; the scan covers at most 100 visible boards.

tools.name: deck_list_labels
tools.title: List Deck labels
tools.description: Lists the labels available on a readable Deck board, with their IDs, titles and colours. Available on Nextcloud 32 through 35 when Deck is enabled.

tools.name: deck_list_card_files
tools.title: List Deck card files
tools.description: Lists only visible existing native file associations of a readable Deck card. Requires deck.read and files.read, Files resource scope, exclusion tags and native node READ. No legacy deck_file or folders, no upload, no hidden count/handle; IDs are association/share IDs distinct from fileId. All visible items ordered by attachmentId; native Card attachmentCount stays omitted. Available on Nextcloud 32 through 35. An association you cannot see is omitted and answered like a missing one. Open the card in Deck without treating that answer as proof that a hidden association exists.

tools.name: talk_list_conversations
tools.title: List Talk conversations
tools.description: Lists the Talk conversations the authenticated user takes part in, with the number of unread messages. It changes no state: it does not mark anything as read, does not touch notifications and does not touch activity.

tools.name: talk_read_messages
tools.title: Read Talk messages
tools.description: Reads conversation messages without changing read or notification state or recording activity. Each page is ordered oldest-to-newest and includes messages plus next_before_message_id. Start without before_message_id; use the returned next_before_message_id as the exclusive before_message_id for older history. The cursor is null when no older page remains. Use a message id in reply_to to answer, and attachmentId to cite an attachment.

modules.title: People
notes: Before acting on a person (inviting, mentioning, messaging), when the user did not give the account ID, call users_search and confirm with the user when more than one account matches. Never invent an ID.
users_search follows the sharing settings of the administrator: it may return nobody for a partial term.

To share something with a whole group, call users_search with include_groups: true and take the ID of the row whose type is "group": a share takes it as group:<id>. Groups are not searched without that argument, and the same administrator restrictions of accounts apply to them.

tools.name: users_search
tools.title: Search people
tools.description: Searches the accounts of this Nextcloud by name, account ID or e-mail and returns their account IDs (uid), display names and, when available, e-mail; every row carries a type, "user" for an account. Use it whenever you are not sure of someone's account ID. Groups are not searched by default: to also match groups, pass include_groups: true, and the group rows come back with the type "group" and the group ID, which is what a share takes as group:<id>.

contents.text:
This guide is in English: relay it to the user in their own language.

Write confirmation plans arrive as readable text in the user’s language, with the complete plan in structuredContent. Show that text to the user exactly as received.

# Tool guide

Grants and disabled apps are already applied: what is missing from this list you cannot call. The modules available to you are files, notes, calendar, contacts, tasks, deck, talk, people.

- **Files** (`files`): 10 tools — List files, Search files, View folder tree, Read file, List file versions, Read file version, View image, View several images, Search images, List shares.
- **Notes** (`notes`): 3 tools — List notes, Search notes, Read note.
- **Calendar** (`calendar`): 2 tools — List calendars, List events.
- **Contacts** (`contacts`): 3 tools — List address books, Search contacts, Read contact.
- **Tasks** (`tasks`): 3 tools — List task calendars, List tasks, Read task.
- **Deck** (`deck`): 7 tools — List Deck boards, List Deck lists, List Deck cards, Read Deck card, Follow up on Deck tasks, List Deck labels, List Deck card files.
- **Talk** (`talk`): 2 tools — List Talk conversations, Read Talk messages.
- **People** (`people`): 1 tools — Search people.

Call this tool again with `module` set to one of those names to get every parameter and every behaviour note of that module, or with `tool` to detail a single tool.

Requires deck.edit and files.read, active editable source and Files scope/tags/node READ; no files.share grant is needed. Revokes this type-12 share for all current/future card members, including a share created by someone else; independent shares may retain access. Preview first, repeat plan_state and the exact file_state receipt with confirm:true. file_state is accepted only on confirm; invalid/replayed/stale receipt, hidden and nonexistent association share one refusal. A confirmed absent association is a no-op only with valid original HMAC and the original file still visible. Never unlinks invisible files, legacy deck_file or folders. Available on Nextcloud 32 through 35. An editor of the card can unlink a visible association created by someone else. A folder you can already see, and an archived card or board, are refused in plain language.

The plan names the file, its owner, whether it is a reshare, the current recipient total, a limited name list and the shares you created. Refuses Guests, group-only sharing, a group or team on the board when group sharing is off, mandatory internal expiry, a recipient that is not a fully resolved local user, group or team, folders, archived cards or boards, and any failure to read those facts. Available on Nextcloud 32 through 35. No upload, copy or file deletion. Native sharing hooks and notifications may run; optional default internal expiry does not apply to this Deck share. Does not suggest changing a sharing policy or signing in another way. A policy enabled later, a membership change, and the gap between the last check and the native share are outside this check: there is no continuous protection and no automatic revocation.

Anyone in the conversation who cannot access the item will see the title and the link, so only reference what the user approves showing. Before sending, the agent MUST call the tool without confirm, which returns a plan and writes nothing, show that plan to the user and ask whether they really want it; only after an explicit yes repeat the same call with confirm: true and the same arguments. Nothing is kept on the server: there is no approval id, no token and no expiry, so the approval itself depends on the agent showing the plan and on the user saying yes in the client.

published.name: talk_send_batch

Use it when the answer is a sequence of short messages (one per item of a list, for instance), and prefer talk_reply when it is a single message. The conversation and the quotes are checked before anything is sent; sending happens item by item and each item is reported in sent or failed, without repeating what was already published. Before sending, the agent MUST call the tool without confirm, which returns a plan and writes nothing, show that plan to the user and ask whether they really want it; only after an explicit yes repeat the same call with confirm: true and the same arguments. published.name: talk_create_group
published.title: Create group in Talk
published.description: Creates a group conversation in Talk, with the authenticated user as its owner: send name with the name of the group and participants with the list of accounts to invite (optional). Every guest goes through the same visibility rule as a direct message, and all of them appear in the preview before any invitation. Creating a group invites people and this tool does not undo an invitation once it has been made, so the operation requires the talk.create grant and an explicit approval. Before sending, the agent MUST call the tool without confirm, which returns a plan and creates nothing, show that plan to the user and ask whether they really want it; only after an explicit yes repeat the same call with confirm: true and the same arguments. Nothing is kept on the server: there is no approval id, no token and no expiry, so the confirmation covers the whole group, name and guests together, and it itself depends on the agent showing the plan and on the user saying yes in the client. Whoever does not approve does not get an empty group in the list: the room is only created by the approved call. The invitations are made one by one after the creation: whoever joined comes in participants and whoever Talk refused comes in invitations_failed, with the id of each one; in that case the group already exists, so do not repeat the call, tell the user who was left out.

The copy is an independent node: does not preserve source id, versions, or shares. Capped at 2000 items and 1073741824 bytes, measured before copying. If source or destination is outside your personal folder, ask the user first and retry with confirm_shared.

definitions.name: files_move
definitions.title: Move file
definitions.description: Move or rename a file or folder within the same file area, without overwriting the destination. Reports id before and after, as well as version and share counts when corresponding apps are enabled. Does not move across different storages: there Nextcloud treats it as a copy and the id changes. If source or destination is outside your personal folder, ask the user first and retry with confirm_shared.

definitions.name: files_move_batch
definitions.title: Move files in bulk
definitions.description: Move several files and create folders, in the given order. Without confirm: true writes nothing and returns the full plan: what would succeed, what conflicts, what Nextcloud denies, what belongs to someone else, and which folders would be created. With confirm: true it executes in order, creates the folders beforehand and returns a batch_id to undo with files_undo_batch. An item failing midway halts the batch: items already moved remain recorded and can be undone, and unattempted items are returned as not_attempted.

definitions.name: files_undo_batch
definitions.title: Undo bulk operation
definitions.description: Undo a files_move_batch, returning each node to its source path in reverse order. Before making any changes checks the whole batch: if any item is no longer what the batch placed at destination, if the source path is already occupied, or if permissions changed, nothing is undone and the response identifies the blocking item. Removes only empty folders that the batch itself created; a folder with content is preserved and listed in kept_dirs.

Passwords are never returned. A room share is a Talk attachment: it is listed with removable: false and is removed in Talk.

definitions.name: files_share
definitions.title: Share file or folder
definitions.description: Share a file or folder of yours with a person or a group, or change how it is already shared with them. Find the account or group id with users_search first (include_groups: true for groups); never guess it. Sharing again with the same recipient changes that share instead of creating another one. permission is view (open and download) or edit (change; on a folder also add and delete inside it); a share never lets the recipient share it on. expires is the last day (YYYY-MM-DD, in the user's timezone, tomorrow or later); omit it to keep the current one, or for a new share to get the administrator's default. Without confirm: true it returns the plan and changes nothing. Nextcloud notifies the recipient. Needs the "share" permission. with: "link" creates or changes your public link on an item you own or can re-share (view only, anyone with it can open it) and needs the "link" permission; use custom_password for a user-chosen password. The server generates one when you pass password: true or the administrator requires one and none was supplied. Only a generated password is returned, once.

Send the bytes with curl -sS -T /tmp/file -X PUT -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" "$UPLOAD_URL"; the answer carries path, size, etag and fileId. Never overwrites a file with content: an existing name is refused, so use files_checkout to replace an existing file. For a small text file use files_create. The folder must exist (files_mkdir creates it); outside your personal folder ask the user and retry with confirm_shared.

Account results carry accountId, the user ID to use for invitations, attendees, Deck and Talk. An empty query lists personal contacts only; accounts need a search term of at least 2 characters.

offset.description: Offset among matching results; use nextOffset to continue.

definitions.name: deck_list_cards

definitions.description: Lists the active cards of a Deck list (stack), paginated.

definitions.name: deck_search_cards
definitions.title: Search Deck cards
definitions.description: Searches active cards on Deck boards you can read by title or description, assignee, labels and due-date range. Results are capped at 100 cards and 2,000 scanned cards; truncated indicates more results or a scan bound.

text.description: Case-insensitive text contained in the card title or description.

assignee.description: UID of the assignee (if you are not sure of someone's ID, call users_search first); returns only the cards assigned to that person.

labelIds.description: Label IDs to match. labelMatch any (default) needs one; all needs every requested label.

labelMatch.description: How labelIds are combined: any requires at least one requested label; all requires every requested label.

dueAfter.description: Returns only cards due on or after this date, in YYYY-MM-DD format, using your account timezone.

dueBefore.description: Returns only cards due on or before this date, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

limit.description: Maximum number of cards to return.

offset.description: Number of matching cards to skip. The scan still stops at 2,000 cards.

definitions.name: deck_read_card
definitions.title: Read Deck card
definitions.description: Reads a Deck card with its description, dates and counters.

definitions.name: deck_create_card
definitions.title: Create card in Deck
definitions.description: Creates a Deck card at the end of a list (stack), owned by you. Optional assignees are account IDs with access to the board; use users_search to resolve IDs. If assignment fails after creation, the created card is returned with a warning. If the resource belongs to somebody else, the agent MUST ask the user before sending confirm_shared: true.

duedate.description: Due date as YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS] in the account timezone, or a timestamp with Z or an explicit offset (±HH:MM). Send null to remove it.

assignees.description: Optional list of account IDs to assign (maximum 100). Each account must exist and have access to the board. Omit or send an empty list to create without explicit assignments.

confirm_shared.description: Set to true only after the user has confirmed the change on somebody else's board.

confirm.description: Send true only after you have shown the plan of this call to the user and the user explicitly said yes. Without it nothing is changed and the answer is the plan.

definitions.name: deck_edit_card
definitions.title: Edit Deck card
definitions.description: Edits the title, description, due date, completion state and assignees of a Deck card. Omit completed to keep its current state; setting it to true or false completes or reopens the card without changing its board position. Repeating true preserves the original completion timestamp. Use assign and unassign (lists of account IDs; use users_search to resolve IDs) to change who is responsible for it. Use lastModified to avoid overwriting a concurrent edit. If an assignment fails midway, the result lists what was assigned, unassigned and failed; nothing is undone. If the resource belongs to somebody else, the agent MUST ask the user before sending confirm_shared: true.

duedate.description: Due date as YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS] in the account timezone, or a timestamp with Z or an explicit offset (±HH:MM). Send null to remove it.

completed.description: Whether the card is complete; omission keeps its current completion state.

assign.description: Optional list of account IDs to assign to the card (maximum 100). Each account must exist and have access to the board. An account already assigned is ignored with a warning. Cannot share an account with unassign.

unassign.description: Optional list of account IDs to remove from the card (maximum 100). An account that is not assigned today is ignored with a warning. Cannot share an account with assign.

lastModified.description: lastModified of the card at the time it was read; if it has changed, the edit is refused.

confirm_shared.description: Set to true only after the user has confirmed the change on somebody else's board.

confirm.description: Send true only after you have shown the plan of this call to the user and the user explicitly said yes. Without it nothing is changed and the answer is the plan.

definitions.name: deck_move_card
definitions.title: Move card in Deck
definitions.description: Moves a Deck card to another list (stack), including one on another board. Without order, the card goes to the end. If the resource belongs to somebody else, the agent MUST ask the user before sending confirm_shared: true.

order.description: Position of the card in the list, from 0 to 99999.

definitions.name: deck_followup_cards
definitions.title: Follow up on Deck tasks
definitions.description: Lists the cards of the boards you can manage (owner or manage permission), grouped by assignee, with a direct link to each card. By default it returns only overdue cards; the scan covers at most 100 visible boards.

status.description: Status filter: overdue (due before today), open, done or all. Default: overdue.

assignee.description: UID of the assignee (if you are not sure of someone's ID, call users_search first); returns only the cards assigned to that person.

dueBefore.description: Returns only cards due on or before this date, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

limit.description: Maximum number of cards to return.

definitions.name: deck_create_board
definitions.title: Create Deck board
definitions.description: Creates a Deck board owned by you, with its lists (stacks) and first cards, in one call and one confirmation: use it to set up a project from scratch instead of creating the pieces one by one. At most 20 lists and 100 cards in total; the cards go to the end of each list, in the order given. The new board is open only to you, so assignees can only be your own account (share the board in Deck first to assign others). If a step fails midway, the result lists what was created and what failed; nothing is undone, so read it before retrying.

color.description: Board colour as six hexadecimal digits, with or without a leading #, for example 0082c9. Default: the Nextcloud blue.

stacks.description: Lists to create on the new board, in order (maximum 20). Each one may carry its first cards (maximum 100 cards in total, in all lists).

cards.description: Cards to create at the end of this list, in order.

duedate.description: Due date as YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS] in the account timezone, or a timestamp with Z or an explicit offset (±HH:MM). Send null to remove it.

assignees.description: Optional list of account IDs to assign (maximum 100). Each account must exist and have access to the board. Omit or send an empty list to create without explicit assignments.

confirm.description: Send true only after you have shown the plan of this call to the user and the user explicitly said yes. Without it nothing is changed and the answer is the plan.

definitions.name: deck_create_stack
definitions.title: Create list in Deck
definitions.description: Creates a list (stack) on a Deck board you manage, at the end or at the given position. To build a whole board with its lists and cards, use deck_create_board. If the resource belongs to somebody else, the agent MUST ask the user before sending confirm_shared: true.

order.description: Position among the lists of the board, from 0 to 99999. Without it the list goes after the last one.

definitions.name: deck_delete_stack
definitions.title: Delete Deck list
definitions.description: Deletes a Deck list (stack), only if it holds no cards, active or archived: move or delete the cards first. Deck moves the list to the trash of the board, where it can be recovered. A card created by someone else right after the second count the tool takes before finishing may go to the trash with the list; it is recoverable there. If the resource belongs to somebody else, the agent MUST ask the user before sending confirm_shared: true.

confirm_shared.description: Set to true only after the user has confirmed the change on somebody else's board.

confirm.description: Send true only after you have shown the plan of this call to the user and the user explicitly said yes. Without it nothing is changed and the answer is the plan.

definitions.name: deck_delete_board
definitions.title: Delete Deck board
definitions.description: Deletes a Deck board you own, only if none of its lists holds a card, active or archived. Its empty lists go with it. Deck moves the board to its trash, where it can be recovered. A card created by someone else right after the second count the tool takes before finishing may go to the trash with the board; it is recoverable there.

Preview first and repeat plan_state with confirm: true. At most 100 IDs per list; duplicates and already satisfied requests are unchanged; an ID cannot occur in both lists. A foreign-board label is refused. Read partial results before any further action. Available on Nextcloud 32 through 35.

definitions.name: deck_list_card_files
definitions.title: List Deck card files
definitions.description: Lists only visible existing native file associations of a readable Deck card. Requires deck.read and files.read, Files resource scope, exclusion tags and native node READ. No legacy deck_file or folders, no upload, no hidden count/handle; IDs are association/share IDs distinct from fileId. All visible items ordered by attachmentId; native Card attachmentCount stays omitted. Available on Nextcloud 32 through 35. An association you cannot see is omitted and answered like a missing one. Open the card in Deck without treating that answer as proof that a hidden association exists.

definitions.name: deck_unlink_card_file
definitions.title: Unlink Deck card file
definitions.description: Unlinks one visible native file association, preserving the original file and other shares. Requires deck.edit and files.read, active editable source and Files scope/tags/node READ; no files.share grant is needed. Revokes this type-12 share for all current/future card members, including a share created by someone else; independent shares may retain access. Preview first, repeat plan_state and the exact file_state receipt with confirm:true. file_state is accepted only on confirm; invalid/replayed/stale receipt, hidden and nonexistent association share one refusal. A confirmed absent association is a no-op only with valid original HMAC and the original file still visible. Never unlinks invisible files, legacy deck_file or folders. Available on Nextcloud 32 through 35. An editor of the card can unlink a visible association created by someone else. A folder you can already see, and an archived card or board, are refused in plain language.

attachmentId.description: Bare native type-12 Deck file share ID returned as attachmentId by deck_list_card_files, not fileId. Legacy deck_file and folders are unsupported.

fileId.description: Original Files node ID from the plan receipt.

createdBy.description: Native share initiator from the plan receipt.

createdAt.description: Native share creation timestamp from the plan receipt.

confirm_shared.description: Set to true only after the user has confirmed the change on somebody else's board.

plan_state.description: Opaque value of the plan. Send it back unchanged together with confirm: true. If the state changed since the plan, nothing is written and the answer is the new plan.

confirm.description: Send true only after you have shown the plan of this call to the user and the user explicitly said yes. Without it nothing is changed and the answer is the plan.

definitions.name: deck_link_card_file
definitions.title: Link Deck card file
definitions.description: Links one existing visible file to a Deck card by a native Deck file share, with read-only access for current and future board members. Requires the three grants deck.edit, files.read and files.share, native EDIT/READ/SHARE, a complete recipient preview and confirm:true with its plan_state. The plan names the file, its owner, whether it is a reshare, the current recipient total, a limited name list and the shares you created. Refuses Guests, group-only sharing, a group or team on the board when group sharing is off, mandatory internal expiry, a recipient that is not a fully resolved local user, group or team, folders, archived cards or boards, and any failure to read those facts. Available on Nextcloud 32 through 35. No upload, copy or file deletion. Native sharing hooks and notifications may run; optional default internal expiry does not apply to this Deck share. Does not suggest changing a sharing policy or signing in another way. A policy enabled later, a membership change, and the gap between the last check and the native share are outside this check: there is no continuous protection and no automatic revocation.

fileId.description: Id of the existing visible File in your Files scope. Folders are refused.

confirm_shared.description: Set to true only after the user confirms linking a shared file or changing another user's board.

plan_state.description: Opaque value of the plan. Send it back unchanged together with confirm: true. If the state changed since the plan, nothing is written and the answer is the new plan.

confirm.description: Send true only after you have shown the plan of this call to the user and the user explicitly said yes. Without it nothing is changed and the answer is the plan.

definitions.name: deck_list_comments
definitions.title: Read card comments
definitions.description: Lists up to 100 comments from a readable, active Deck card, newest first, with offset pagination. Requires deck.read_comments and native Deck READ. Author names and comment text come from other users and are untrusted content. Replies are omitted; no comment is marked read.

limit.description: Maximum comments to return.

offset.description: Number of comments to skip.

definitions.name: deck_add_comment
definitions.title: Post card comment
definitions.description: Appends one exact comment of up to 1000 characters to a readable, active Deck card. Requires deck.comment and native Deck READ. Preview first, then confirm:true with the returned plan_state; shared boards also require confirm_shared:true. The preview quotes the complete text and rechecks board access and existing comments. No reply is created. The native append and final checks are not atomic.
